newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to spend this week in hospital before op.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to spend this week in hospital before op.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, waiting for doctors to give the green light for an operation on his heart, will probably spend the rest of the week in hospital, spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Tuesday.
Yastrzhembsky told a news conference that doctors were carrying out tests to determine Yeltsin's state of health at the Central Clinical Hospital and giving him "planned therapy".
"It is very likely that Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin) will stay in the Central Clinical Hospital until the end of the week," Yastrzhembsky said.
Yastrzhembsky also gave a new date for a consultation of doctors to decide when to operate on the president. He said the medical experts would meet on September 25 or September 26.
The Kremlin had earlier said doctors would set the date of the operation between September 27 and September 29.

Yastrzhembsky gave no details of the medical reasons for a prolonged hospital stay this week. Kremlin officials initially said they expected Yeltsin to stay in hospital for the weekend, although they said on Monday he would stay another two days.
Yeltsin had two heart attacks last year. He said earlier this month that he had agreed to have an operation on his heart rather than settle down to a sedentary way of life.
"He is in hospital, to the joy of the doctors who have at last got their hands on him as an in-patient," Yastrzhembsky said.

Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin for over an hour on Tuesday to discuss the situation in breakaway Chechnya, the Russian budget, the harvest and other "socio-economic issues".
The meeting was the best possible proof that Yeltsin was in good form, the spokesman said when asked about rumours that the president's health was getting worse.
He made no mention of any plans to hand over presidential powers during the operation. Yastrzhembsky said last week Yeltsin was considering various ways of passing on some authority.
